source_signature.notes: Batch 4H skill 4/4, BATCH CLOSER (four-skill exception). Scope Operator-derived. The unwrapped-wedge specialization: a square thread is an inclined plane wrapped around a cylinder of mean radius r; unwrapping one turn gives a right triangle with base 2*pi*r and rise L, so the lead angle theta FROM THE HORIZONTAL satisfies tan theta = L/(2*pi*r), and the screw analysis is the wedge analysis on that incline with the applied moment M replacing the wedge driving force. wedge_friction (signed same batch) is cited as the direct analogy, not re-solved; coulomb_friction_impending supplies F = mu_s N at impending; dry_friction_static_kinetic and friction_fbd_normal_force are the signed single-surface parallel. Excluded: belt friction, rolling resistance, collar/journal bearing friction, thread stress, screw efficiency/power design. FRICTION DISTINCTION BITES: the impending-motion premise is stated (slip impends at the thread, so |F| = mu_s N holds AT THE LIMIT - not the reflexive F = muN in every statics problem), and friction DIRECTION opposes the impending RELATIVE motion of the thread surfaces, not the applied moment - raising puts friction DOWN the unwrapped incline, lowering FLIPS it UP, and that flip is shown to be what CHANGES the tangent argument from theta+phi_s to phi_s-theta rather than the arguments being asserted from memorized formulas. Worked example Operator-re-derived (source-locked to the on-disk prompt): square-threaded screw jack, r = 25 mm, single-start lead L = 10 mm, mu_s = 0.20, W = 5000 N. tan theta = 10/(2*pi*25) = 1/(5*pi) = 0.063662 -> theta = 3.64 deg (ratio NOT inverted); tan phi_s = 0.20 -> phi_s = 11.31 deg (friction angle referenced from the surface normal; both angle references stated and distinct). RAISING: tan(theta+phi_s) = (0.063662+0.20)/(1-0.063662*0.20) = 0.267063 -> M_raise = 5000*0.025*0.267063 = 33.4 N.m. SELF-LOCKING: phi_s 11.31 deg > theta 3.64 deg (equivalently mu_s 0.20 > tan theta 0.0637), so the screw holds the load with no applied moment and lowering still requires a moment. LOWERING: tan(phi_s-theta) = (0.20-0.063662)/(1+0.20*0.063662) = 0.134624 -> M_lower = 16.8 N.m. Both distinguishing decisions are exercised - the self-locking test AND the lowering moment - so a raising-only plug-in is detectably incomplete; M_lower < M_raise with both positive, correct for a self-locking screw. TRIG-RESOLUTION CROSS-CHECK APPLIED and PASSED (standing rule from the Batch 4G finding): both angle references explicitly stated, the lead ratio not inverted, tangent addition and subtraction identities verified numerically. THREE-signal mapping under AXIOMIQ_CANONICAL_FAILURE_SIGNAL_VOCABULARY_V1: axis_confusion at step 3 (angle-reference assignment - measuring theta from the vertical, confusing theta with phi_s, or inverting tan theta = L/(2*pi*r); a reference-assignment earn), sign_or_placement_error at step 6 (the raising/lowering friction-direction flip - opposing the applied moment instead of impending relative motion, or swapping the tangent arguments), unclassified at step 7 (boundary fallback, content-earned: a raising-only plug-in that never touches the flip or self-locking, reflexive muN, or reaching into belt/rolling/bearing/stress/efficiency). solution_sequencing_error OMITTED: theta and phi_s are independent prerequisite computations feeding one moment expression - no authored step exposes an out-of-order solve that strands an unknown, unlike wedge_friction's two-body coupling where the wedge FBD is underdetermined without the load body. simple_average_used omitted (Centroids-family only). CLOSES BATCH 4H at 53/98: internal_force_sign_convention, torque_internal_loading, wedge_friction, screw_friction.
